replaces.change: Three eggs instead of two for protein; soy sauce cut to 1 tbsp and ginger + sesame carry the flavor (bundled math sat near 480 mg sodium/serving, this lands lower); explicit day-old-rice guidance; thermometer doneness for the eggs; named equipment

qty.note: cooked and chilled first - about 1 3/4 cups cooked; day-old leftover rice is ideal for fried rice

steps.text: Break the eggs into a bowl, add a pinch of the salt, and beat with chopsticks or a fork until completely uniform.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the vegetable oil in a wok over medium-high heat until it shimmers.

Pour in the eggs and let them puff for a few seconds, then push gently with the spatula into soft curds. If you check with a thermometer, the eggs are safe at 160°F (71°C) — they will look just set, still glossy.

safety.source: USDA FSIS safe minimum internal temperature table

steps.text: Slide the eggs onto a plate while the centers are still slightly wet.
Add the remaining oil, then the ginger and garlic. Stir for 30 seconds until fragrant — pull the wok off the heat if the garlic browns.
Add the cold rice and break every clump with the spatula. Press it into an even layer and leave it alone for 1 minute to toast the bottom.
Toss and stir-fry for 2 minutes, until the rice is steaming hot and smells nutty.
Drizzle the soy sauce and sesame oil down the hot side of the wok, add the peas, and toss for 1 minute until the peas are steaming.
Return the eggs, add the green onions, and fold twice — keep the curds in big pieces.
Taste, add white pepper and more salt only if it needs it, and serve straight from the wok.

nutrition_per_serving.basis: USDA FoodData Central values committed in apps/ios/Resources/usda_ingredient_catalog.sqlite (matched fdc_id per ingredient in tables/nutrition-map.json), plus the app's shipped core-ingredient table (data.json) for items without an fdc_id; scaled by evidenced gram quantities
